name: Question 5
problem:
Compute the standard deviation $\sigma $ of the following data set:

$$
-11,\,2,\,1,\,9,\,-10,\,1,\,-13
$$

Do not round your answer.

$\sigma =$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a data set ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is the square root of the variance:

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2}}=\sqrt{\,\,\,\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-{(\overset{―}{x})}^{2}}
$$

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=7$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (-11+2+1+9-10+1-13) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (-21) \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot [(-11)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{9}^{2}+(-10)^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-13)^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot [121+4+1+81+100+1+169] \\  & =\frac{477}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{477}{7}-{(-3)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{477}{7}-9 \\  & =\frac{477-63}{7} \\  & =\frac{414}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the standard deviation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\sigma  & =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}} \\  & =3\sqrt{\frac{46}{7}}.\end{aligned}
$$
